The fixture window is 3 hunks and contains no assertion at all -- it is deliberately narrow so that a non-zero could only come from the literal, and that narrowness is also why it cannot speak to how the counter behaves when a register edit shares a hunk with an assertion edit.
A positive control's strength is bounded by whether the control could have failed. It could: C is in the same path shape with the same literals in the same file, and it stayed at 0.
the_finding: `register-lines-only` went 0 -> 1 on a hunk that DELETED a `("src/foo.rs", 1234),` tuple, 0 -> 1 on a hunk that ADDED `("src/baz.rs", 777),`, and stayed 0 on a hunk in the same path shape with the same tuples present only as CONTEXT lines. Both before/after directions fire, in both scan modes, and the near-miss stays dark. So the counter's positive signal is reachable by a fixture I built outside my repository's history, and the flat 17-vs-0 is no longer explained by 'the census cannot fire on anyone else'.
the_world_the_outcome_selects: IN THE PRE-REGISTRATION'S OWN WORDS, the branch that fired is: 'If the register hunk FIRES and the control hunk does NOT, then the ripgrep 0 means world 2 is falsified for this row: the counter has reach beyond my own repository.' So the ripgrep `register-lines-only 0` is a zero from a counter DEMONSTRATED CAPABLE of firing outside my own history, and it is weak evidence in world 1's direction -- that a `("path.rs", N)` debt register is a habit of MINE rather than a generic Rust idiom. The OTHER pre-registered branch that would have fired on a miss ('then my reading of the trigger condition is wrong, and the 17 is UNREPRODUCED, not yet SUSPECT') did NOT fire, so the 17 needs no audit on this ground. The third branch ('if the CONTROL hunk fires too, the counter is not discriminating on the literal at all and the row is not a measurement') did NOT fire either: C scored 0 in both modes, so the row is NOT merely counting 'non-assert test-file hunks that produced no finding'.

The ripgrep 0 is now read as a zero from a LIVE counter, never as evidence that ripgrep keeps no register. IT SAYS NOTHING ABOUT THE OVER/UNDER-COUNT COUPLING recorded in section 1 of the md file. `count_register_lines` re-calls `classify_assertion_change` and skips any hunk that is IN scope, so (a) a register churn that travels with a RECOGNISED assertion edit is NOT counted (under-count), and (b) a foreign hunk carrying an UNREADABLE oracle AND a register literal is counted (over-count). A fixture cannot measure how often either happens in a real history; both remain live confounds for every foreign 0.

IT DOES NOT LICENSE THE 17. The 17 hunks in my own history are still a tally over survivors of the published instrument, and they have NOT been read individually. This fixture corroborates the MECHANISM, not those hunks -- all 17 could be register-shaped data edits that are not debt registers at all and this result would be unchanged.
